study_identification.author_journal_year: Mao et al., Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience, 2025
study_identification.title: Mapping early corpus callosum development to identify neurodevelopmental risk

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study investigated early childhood corpus callosum development, a critical process for cognitive maturation and implicated in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), using sex-specific growth curve models. These findings establish sex-specific corpus callosum growth curve models as a quantitative, generalizable tool for characterizing typical development and detecting atypical morphometry, offering a promising approach for early, objective ASD diagnosis and potentially facilitating timely intervention.

quality_checking_detail.answer: CAT12 toolbox (IQR <= 'C-' exclusion) and manual inspection with ITK-SNAP. 18 images were excluded.

response_variable.answer: Corpus callosum morphometrics: area, length, perimeter, circularity, total volume, and volumes of anterior, mid-anterior, central, mid-posterior, and posterior subregions.

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex as fixed effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.answer: The normative model was constructed using data from a single scanner to avoid site effects. Sex-specific models were created.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.answer: The model was validated on an independent dataset acquired on a different scanner (3T Philips vs. 1.5T Siemens for the training set) to assess generalizability.

deviation_metric.answer: Percentile scores; Outliers (>90th or <10th percentile); Mahalanobis distance

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Regularized discriminant analysis (RDA) classifiers were trained to distinguish between ASD and TDC using deviation scores. Performance was assessed with 10-fold cross-validation, reporting mean classification accuracy and AUC.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Classifiers trained on deviations from the growth curves accurately distinguished children with ASD from TDC (mean AUC = 0.95), demonstrating model generalizability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The classifier achieved a mean AUC of 0.95. Classifiers using only subregion volumes or only sagittal plane features achieved AUCs of 0.916 and 0.894, respectively. The median Mahalanobis distance was significantly greater in the ASD group (42.65) compared to the TDC group (9.42).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study used a cross-sectional design, the control group was recruited from a clinical population, and the peak developmental ages were based on extrapolations beyond the study's age range.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The model's high accuracy on data from a different scanner suggests good generalizability, a crucial feature for clinical applications.

general_notes.general_notes: A key feature of this study is the deliberate use of a different scanner for the validation dataset to stringently test the generalizability of the normative model.
